bull.b: AI infrastructure demand is expanding Teradyne’s semiconductor test opportunity, while strong compute growth and hyperscaler engagement support sustained adoption. This broadens the company’s exposure to durable data-center investment and can reinforce share gains over the next several years.

Consistently high gross and operating margins indicate differentiated test platforms, valuable software and services, and operating leverage. These levels provide resources for continued R&D and commercialization while supporting durable earnings power across the cycle.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet and positive cash generation
bull.b: Very low leverage limits financial strain and preserves flexibility for R&D, capacity, acquisitions or shareholder returns. Positive free cash flow and substantial cash balances strengthen resilience when semiconductor spending weakens or customers delay equipment purchases.

bear.b: Teradyne remains exposed to semiconductor and electronics capital-spending cycles, so revenue can contract sharply between technology ramps. Uneven historical growth reduces earnings visibility and makes sustained expansion dependent on customer investment timing and end-market demand.

bear.t: Memory mix and investment pressure on margins
bear.b: Memory growth can expand the addressable market but currently carries margin pressure, while higher R&D, go-to-market spending and compensation raise the cost base. Persistent mix and investment effects could limit operating-margin expansion despite strong demand.

bear.t: Execution, inventory and qualification timing risk
bear.b: Building inventory ahead of demand can tie up cash and increase the risk of mismatched supply if customer ramps shift. Long qualification cycles, dual sourcing and supply-chain friction may also delay conversions and make market-share gains less predictable.
